title: Majestic Zugzwang
summary: Let Black promote, then use the king to close the queen’s last safe squares.

nodes.question: Can White afford to let Black promote?
nodes.explanation: White has two knights and an h-pawn against two advanced pawns. Moving the h2 knight to f1 attacks g3 and leaves the e3 knight ready to recapture on f1.

nodes.question: Where should the king go after the queen appears?
nodes.explanation: The queen on g1 looks powerful, but both knights and the h4 pawn already cover most of its exits. White must complete that cage without disturbing the knights.

branches.title: Allow a queen, then close the cage
commentary: Begin from the complete seven-piece source diagram. Selected promotion branches are encoded; this is not a claim to enumerate all Black defenses.
Nhf1 moves the attacked h2 knight to f1 and attacks g3. The other knight stays on e3 to protect f1.
g2 advances the attacked pawn toward promotion. This is the source’s selected response.
h4 starts the distant passer and controls g5. White deliberately leaves both promotion squares available.
g1=Q avoids the immediate capture on f1 and creates the source’s queen-cage challenge.
Kf7 covers g6, g7 and g8. Together with the knights and h-pawn, it leaves the queen without a safe escape; the king and f2 pawn are also blocked.
Qxf1 removes one knight but gives up the queen. This is the illustrated capture, not the queen’s only legal move.
Nxf1 recaptures with the knight from e3. The queen is gone and White can blockade f2 with the surviving knight.
Kg2 frees the corner and attacks the knight on f1, forcing White to reposition it.
Nd2 moves the knight to a square controlling f1. Black cannot safely promote the pawn there.
Kg3 heads toward the h-pawn but cannot catch it in this exact position.
h5 advances the protected winning plan. The exact tablebase still gives White a win; the remaining race is not invented here.
branches.explanation: h5 advances the protected winning plan. The exact tablebase still gives White a win; the remaining race is not invented here.

branches.title: Promote by capturing the knight
commentary: Compare Black’s illustrated promotion with capture instead of creating a queen on g1.
Nhf1 attacks the g3 pawn and is protected by Ne3.
g2 brings that pawn one step from promotion.
h4 creates the distant passer while keeping both knights in place.
gxf1=Q captures the knight and promotes, but the new queen lands on a square guarded by Ne3.
Nxf1 removes the new queen immediately. White retains the distant pawn and a knight able to stop f2.
Kg2 attacks that knight, trying to release the f-pawn.
Nd2 retreats while controlling f1, maintaining the blockade.
Kg3 approaches the h-file too late to stop the checked winning race.
h5 advances toward promotion. White’s exact win is checked at this endpoint rather than inferred from material alone.
branches.explanation: h5 advances toward promotion. White’s exact win is checked at this endpoint rather than inferred from material alone.

exercises.prompt: Why move the king away from the pawns?
exercises.answer: Kf7 closes g6, g7 and g8, the queen’s upper exits. The knights and h-pawn cover the lower exits, forcing Black to give something up.

exercises.prompt: Why can the remaining knight stop f2?
exercises.answer: After ...Qxf1 Nxf1 ...Kg2, Nd2 controls f1. The knight changes blockade square while the h-pawn races.

startContext: The complete seven-piece opening board is reconstructed from the saved images. The two illustrated queen-promotion choices and selected king/knight replies are checked move by move. Safe-square coverage explains Kf7; no exhaustive defense tree is claimed.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
